q-162907.name: Question 1
q-162907.worked_solution:
First, we put the numerator and denominator under separate radicals and then simplify the result:

$$
\sqrt{\frac{16{d}^{2}}{49}}=\frac{\sqrt{16{d}^{2}}}{\sqrt{49}}=\frac{\sqrt{16{d}^{2}}}{\sqrt{{7}^{2}}}=\frac{\sqrt{16{d}^{2}}}{7}
$$

Now, notice that the expression inside the radical is a perfect square. So, we can continue simplifying by writing the expression as this perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{16{d}^{2}}}{7} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{(4d)^{2}}}{7} & = \\ \frac{|4d|}{7} & = \\ \frac{|4|\cdot |d|}{7} & = \\ \frac{4\cdot |d|}{7} & = \\ \frac{4|d|}{7}\end{aligned}
$$

q-162911.name: Question 2
q-162911.worked_solution:
First, we put the numerator and denominator under separate radicals and then simplify the result:

$$
\sqrt{\frac{81}{16{k}^{2}}}=\frac{\sqrt{81}}{\sqrt{16{k}^{2}}}=\frac{\sqrt{{9}^{2}}}{\sqrt{16{k}^{2}}}=\frac{9}{\sqrt{16{k}^{2}}}
$$

Now, notice that the expression inside the radical is a perfect square. So, we can continue simplifying by writing the expression as this perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{9}{\sqrt{16{k}^{2}}} & = \\ \frac{9}{\sqrt{(4k)^{2}}} & = \\ \frac{9}{|4k|} & = \\ \frac{9}{|4|\cdot |k|} & = \\ \frac{9}{4\cdot |k|} & = \\ \frac{9}{4|k|}\end{aligned}
$$

q-162926.name: Question 3
q-162926.worked_solution:
First, we put the numerator and denominator under separate radicals and then simplify the result:

$$
\sqrt{\frac{4{z}^{4}}{49}}=\frac{\sqrt{4{z}^{4}}}{\sqrt{49}}=\frac{\sqrt{4{z}^{4}}}{\sqrt{{7}^{2}}}=\frac{\sqrt{4{z}^{4}}}{7}
$$

Now, notice that the expression inside the radical is a perfect square. So, we can continue simplifying by writing the expression as this perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{4{z}^{4}}}{7} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{(2{z}^{2})^{2}}}{7} & = \\ \frac{|2{z}^{2}|}{7} & = \\ \frac{|2|\cdot |{z}^{2}|}{7} & = \\ \frac{2\cdot |{z}^{2}|}{7}\end{aligned}
$$

A squared number is always positive or zero, and the absolute value of any positive (or zero) number is itself, so we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2\cdot |{z}^{2}|}{7} & = \\ \frac{2\cdot {z}^{2}}{7} & = \\ \frac{2{z}^{2}}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-162932.name: Question 4
q-162932.worked_solution:
First, we bring the quotient under a single radical and then simplify the result:

$$
\frac{\sqrt{12{a}^{4}}}{\sqrt{3}}=\sqrt{\frac{12{a}^{4}}{3}}=\sqrt{4{a}^{4}}
$$

Now, notice that the expression inside the radical is a perfect square. So, we can continue simplifying by writing the expression as this perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{4{a}^{4}} & = \\ \sqrt{(2{a}^{2})^{2}} & = \\ |2{a}^{2}| & = \\ |2|\cdot |{a}^{2}| & = \\ 2\cdot |{a}^{2}|\end{aligned}
$$

A squared number is always positive or zero, and the absolute value of any positive (or zero) number is itself, so we have

$$
\begin{aligned}2\cdot |{a}^{2}| & = \\ 2\cdot {a}^{2} & = \\ 2{a}^{2}.\end{aligned}

q-3094.name: Question 5
q-3094.worked_solution:
First, we bring the quotient under a single radical and then simplify the result:

$$
\frac{\sqrt{8{x}^{3}}}{\sqrt{50x}}=\sqrt{\frac{8{x}^{3}}{50x}}=\sqrt{\frac{4{x}^{2}}{25}}
$$

Now, notice that the expression inside the radical is a perfect square. So, we can continue simplifying by writing the expression as this perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{\frac{4{x}^{2}}{25}} & = \\ \sqrt{{(\frac{2x}{5})}^{2}} & = \\ |\frac{2x}{5}| & = \\ \frac{|2x|}{|5|} & = \\ \frac{|2|\cdot |x|}{5} & = \\ \frac{2\cdot |x|}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Lastly, we are told that $x>0,$ so we have $|x|=x.$ Therefore, the final answer is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2\cdot |x|}{5} & = \\ \frac{2\cdot x}{5} & = \\ \frac{2x}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-162959.name: Question 6
q-162959.worked_solution:
First, we put the numerator and denominator under separate radicals and then simplify the result:

$$
\sqrt{\frac{36}{121{t}^{2}}}=\frac{\sqrt{36}}{\sqrt{121{t}^{2}}}=\frac{\sqrt{{6}^{2}}}{\sqrt{121{t}^{2}}}=\frac{6}{\sqrt{121{t}^{2}}}
$$

Now, notice that the expression inside the radical is a perfect square. So, we can continue simplifying by writing the expression as this perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{6}{\sqrt{121{t}^{2}}} & = \\ \frac{6}{\sqrt{(11t)^{2}}} & = \\ \frac{6}{|11t|} & = \\ \frac{6}{|11|\cdot |t|} & = \\ \frac{6}{11\cdot |t|}\end{aligned}
$$

Lastly, we are told that $t<0,$ so we have $|t|=-t.$ Therefore, the final answer is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{6}{11\cdot |t|} & = \\ \frac{6}{11\cdot (-t)} & = \\ -\frac{6}{11t}.\end{aligned}
$$
